data.title: Roger Goodell Agrees To Four-Year NFL Contract Extension Through 2030 Season
data.description: According to CNBC, NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell has agreed to a four-year contract extension that runs through the 2030 league season and ends on March 31, 2031. The NFL's Compensation Committee notified full ownership of the deal on Sunday, and New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft said the agreement is heavily performance-based, with more than 95% of total compensation tied to Goodell's and the league's performance against various metrics. Financial terms were not immediately known. Kraft, who chairs the compensation committee, said the committee worked with an independent third-party compensation consultant and outside counsel to structure the contract around the NFL's long-term interests and success. Goodell's extension is his fifth since becoming commissioner in 2006.

data.title: Polymarket Milwaukee Brewers Odds Drop to 14.5% in Reds Matchup
data.description: Polymarket’s "Milwaukee Brewers vs. Cincinnati Reds" submarket saw the Milwaukee Brewers option’s implied win probability swing sharply from 57.5% one hour earlier to 14.5% at the time of monitoring, a 43% move. According to ChainCatcher, the sudden change may reflect the impact of breaking news.

data.title: Energy Secretary Cautiously Predicts Lower Gasoline Prices After Labor Day
data.description: According to Axios, Energy Secretary Chris Wright said Sunday that lower gasoline prices would not be an unreasonable expectation, but he stopped short of making a firm or precise forecast. Wright said on CBS's "Face the Nation" and CNN's "State of the Union" that U.S. gasoline demand typically falls after Labor Day as the summer driving season ends, while gasoline production is set to rise. He also cited recent administration moves to ease some environmental requirements for summer gasoline blends and pointed to lower gasoline futures prices in coming months. U.S. regular gasoline averaged $4.15 per gallon on Sunday, according to AAA data, while diesel prices were at all-time highs and crude oil was trading at its highest level in roughly six weeks, with the global benchmark above $96 per barrel at Friday's close.

data.title: Berlin Refuses 30 BTC Rhysida Ransom, Hackers Leak 5.7 Terabytes
data.description:
Berlin’s state government refused to pay a 30 Bitcoin ransom demanded by the Rhysida ransomware group, and the hackers published 5.7 terabytes of stolen data on the dark web after the deadline passed. According to BeInCrypto, the State of Berlin said it would not give in to blackmail, while officials warned residents’ personal data could be included in the leak.

The attack surfaced on August 14, and Berlin’s Senate Chancellery valued the demand at about two million euros. The State Criminal Police Office and Germany’s federal cybersecurity agency are leading the investigation.

data.title: Trump Administration Renews Supreme Court Appeal Over Mail Ballot Restrictions
data.description: According to CNBC, the Trump administration on Sunday renewed its appeal to the Supreme Court after a federal judge blocked new restrictions on mail ballots ahead of the midterms. U.S. District Court Judge Indira Talwani had extended an order barring the Postal Service from enforcing President Donald Trump's executive order for the November elections. Solicitor General John Sauer said in the filing that ballots had already begun to be mailed in North Carolina and that more states would start sending them out, including Alabama on September 9 and at least five states the week of September 13. The administration said the injunction could create confusion and chaos, while Democratic states and voting rights groups argued the changes are unconstitutional and election officials said they do not have enough time to revise their systems. The filing also said eligibility for mail-in and absentee voting will continue to be governed by state law, and that the Postal Service will not determine voter eligibility, maintain voter rolls or count ballots.

data.description:

data.title: U.S. Energy Secretary Says Navy Will Continue Escorting Tankers Through the Strait of Hormuz
data.description: According to Jin10, U.S. Energy Secretary Wright said on Sunday that U.S. Navy escort vessels are helping tankers pass through the Strait of Hormuz and that the escort operation will not end soon. Wright said the Navy is ensuring that many ships pass through the waterway, that U.S. military involvement is necessary, and that Iran is still causing trouble, but the U.S. Navy is winning the battle. He said the average daily volume of oil passing through the Strait of Hormuz is now more than 9 million barrels, and that the region's oil transport volume has recovered to two-thirds or more of its pre-conflict level as more crude oil and refined products move through pipelines and other routes. Last week, Wright said about 17 million barrels of oil passed through the Strait of Hormuz on Monday. Wright also said unleaded gasoline prices may fall as the summer driving season ends and federal blending policy adjustments increase supply.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | NBA Fines Clippers $30 Million, Takes Five First-Round Picks
data.description:
The NBA fined the Los Angeles Clippers $30 million and stripped the team of five first-round draft picks after an independent investigation found it circumvented salary-cap rules by facilitating off-court income opportunities for Kawhi Leonard, according to Bloomberg.

Owner Steve Ballmer was suspended for a year, and Leonard was fined $700,000 in one of the league’s most severe disciplinary actions.

data.title: U.S. Energy Secretary: Strait of Hormuz Oil Flows Top 9 Million Barrels a Day
data.description: According to Sina Finance, U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright said daily oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz average more than 9 million barrels, and total oil transport capacity, including alternative pipelines, has recovered to at least two-thirds of pre-conflict levels. He added that Iran is still causing trouble, but the U.S. Navy is winning the contest.

data.title: Harmony Proposes Mainnet Shutdown, ONE Migration to Ethereum, and AI Video Business Shift
data.description:
Harmony has proposed two non-binding plans to shut down its mainnet, migrate the native ONE token to Ethereum, and shift into an AI video remix business. According to PANews, the team said threats from state-level attackers and AI agents were the reasons for proposing the network shutdown.

The migration plan would take a snapshot at the network's final block of user wallets, staking delegations, validator rewards, smart contracts, and tokens held on centralized exchanges. New ONE would be airdropped on Ethereum to the same wallet addresses without requiring holders to claim it, while delegated staking and unclaimed rewards would be airdropped to the respective governance treasuries. The total ONE supply and issuance rate would remain unchanged, and newly issued tokens would be used for the new business.

Harmony said multisig wallets, liquidity pools, and on-chain applications cannot migrate, and urged users to exit all smart contracts by September 10, 2026. The team also plans to publish the token contract, snapshot calculations, and airdrop scripts for audit. Validators can stop running nodes starting at 22:00 (UTC+8) on September 10.

The team plans to compensate the difference in issuance rewards between node shutdown and the network's final block, and has set aside a one-time compensation pool of $1.372 million. Payments would be made over four quarters to validators and delegators who stop on time, sign the agreement, keep their stake, and serve as governors for the new project.

The new business would allow users to remix prompts and materials, with AI agents expanding video stories. Harmony also plans to recruit operators for video generation, distribution, and content review. In the first year, the company plans to subsidize GPU hardware and support video generation demand, while operators would stake tokens and earn rewards based on service uptime. The team said operators could generate up to $1 million in combined first-year revenue if staking and uptime requirements are met, and promoters could receive a 30% ongoing commission from their referrals' monthly $10 subscriptions.

data.title: PPP Monitoring Shows Loss-Making Account Bought MOUZ Win Prediction in CS2 Blast Final
data.description:
PPP monitoring showed that an account with nearly $200,000 in losses bought a MOUZ win prediction for the CS2 Blast final against Spirit. According to Odaily, the wallet address 0x7c37b52eb226bcb9411375ec48b0169663fb6aeb opened the position at an average price of 36.4 cents and bought 786,825.9 shares.

The match began at 22:00 on September 6 and was played as a best-of-five series. Spirit was described as a top team, while MOUZ reached the final after a 2-0 semifinal win over Team Vitality.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Haley Stevens Says Canadian Tariffs Are Raising Costs in Michigan
data.description:
Michigan Representative Haley Stevens said escalating US tariffs on Canadian goods are raising costs and creating uncertainty for manufacturers in her district, with the auto supply chain especially exposed, according to Bloomberg.

She told Bloomberg This Weekend hosts Christina Ruffini and Jeff Mason that she is promoting legislation to provide households with as much as $1,700 to offset tariff-related costs, while criticizing the Trump administration’s trade approach with Canada.

data.title: BOC Fund Names Chen Weixing Executive President
data.description:
BOC Fund said on September 5 that former chief inspector and deputy executive president Chen Weixing has been appointed executive president, effective September 4. After stepping down from his previous roles, the chief inspector post remains vacant and Chen will continue to act in that capacity, according to Jiemian News.

The move follows the departure of former executive president Zhang Jiawen on August 10, when he left for a planned role as executive president of BOC Investment (Hong Kong). Chen joined BOC Fund in 2022. Public records show he previously worked at Bank of China headquarters and branches in several senior roles.

Jiemian News also reported that BOC Fund’s management has been updated again after Liu Xinqun formally became chairman and legal representative on December 11, 2025. Wind data showed the firm’s public fund assets under management reached 731.716 billion yuan at the end of the second quarter of 2026, a record high. Of that, money market funds accounted for 453.503 billion yuan, non-money market funds for 278.112 billion yuan, bond funds for 233.361 billion yuan, hybrid funds for 21.993 billion yuan and equity funds for 9.048 billion yuan.

As of the end of the second quarter, BOC Fund managed 334 public funds, with 145 products above 200 million yuan each and 11 funds above 10 billion yuan each. It had 113 active equity funds, including 59 so-called mini funds with less than 50 million yuan each. Jiemian News reported that the firm launched 14 funds so far this year, including four active hybrid funds with initial sizes of 66 million yuan, 10 million yuan, 16 million yuan and 15 million yuan.
